mechanism: The handler opens with (unless (and (listp inputs) (> (length inputs) 0)) (error ... :message "Invalid inputs")) at src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:847-849, so both spellings of an empty array are refused: a top-level [] arrives as the +json-empty-array+ sentinel, which is not a list, and an explicit null arrives as NIL, whose length is 0. Core's AddInputs (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/rawtransaction_util.cpp:25-33) treats a null or empty inputs array as zero inputs and loops zero times, and ConstructTransaction (:147-171) imposes no minimum. Because the guard runs before PARSE-OUTPUTS, the outputs argument is never parsed at all when inputs is empty.
consequence: createrawtransaction([], {...}) is the standard way to build an unsigned funding template and appears at 33 call sites across Core's functional tests (grep for createrawtransaction([ ] and the inputs=[ ] keyword spelling); here it is a hard -8, so that workflow is unavailable through this RPC. It also collapses eight of Core's outputs-argument diagnostics into one wrong message: rpc_rawtransaction.py:293-302 drives 'Data must be hexadecimal string', 'Invalid Bitcoin address', 'Invalid amount', 'Amount out of range' and the two duplicate-key messages all through an empty inputs array, and every one of them answers 'Invalid inputs' instead. The failure is loud and produces no artifact a caller can act on - no wrong fee, transaction or address - so the mechanism is confirmed and the severity is S3 rather than the S2 it was filed at. Worth noting it does not break our own funding path: createpsbt and walletcreatefundedpsbt build through %PSBT-BUILD-UNSIGNED-TX, which accepts an empty inputs list.
evidence: Probe ga11v-rpcutil-p1 (scratch, not committed), through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method with bl.rpc::%normalize-rpc-params so the empty array reaches the handler exactly as a JSON-RPC client sends it: params #(#() (<data output>)) -> (:RPC-ERROR -8 'Invalid inputs'), and the null spelling (nil (<data output>)) -> the same. The identical output argument succeeds when one input is supplied, so the -8 is the inputs guard and not an outputs problem. Ours: src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:843-849; the sentinel is src/rpc/server.lisp:110-133. Core at d3056bc: rpc/rawtransaction_util.cpp:25-33,147-171; test/functional/rpc_rawtransaction.py:293-302; 33 lines matching createrawtransaction([]) or createrawtransaction(inputs=[]) across test/functional/.
fix_shape: Delete the minimum-length half of the guard and accept zero inputs, keeping only a type check that mirrors Core's: a null or empty array means no inputs, anything that is not an array is -3 'JSON value of type ... is not of expected type array'. Read the argument through BL.RPC:POSITIONAL-ARRAY so the +json-empty-array+ sentinel becomes the empty list, which is what createpsbt already does at src/wallet/psbt.lisp:110 with a comment naming this exact trap - the lesson json-null-vs-empty-array-sentinel-is-truthy is the same one. Order matters as much as the guard: Core parses locktime, then version, then inputs, then outputs, so once inputs may be empty the outputs diagnostics become reachable and rpc_rawtransaction.py:293-302 can be used as the acceptance test.
